clue.text: Travellers shortly going to see this standard raised ?

definitions.text: Travellers shortly going to see this standard raised ?

parts.words: Travellers shortly going to see this standard raised
parts.note: a flag hoisted on a ship to announce that it will sail soon, so travellers aboard are about to go to sea

explanation.surface: A banner goes up for tourists about to set off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag, not a level of quality: the blue-and-white signal flag hoisted in harbour to show a ship is about to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue flag with a white square is the naval signal that a vessel is ready to put to sea.

clue.text: Glass or beer-mat needs changing

indicators.note: the letters of the words before need changing round into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether a pint glass or the coaster under it should be swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass' sits beside 'beer-mat' as if it were a drinking vessel; here it is the old word for the weather instrument. 'needs changing' rearranges OR and BEERMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather glass is the traditional name for the instrument measuring air pressure.

clue.text: Golf club not opening, say ?

indicators.note: the club's name loses its opening letter, the one at the front

parts.note: a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer asks whether a club that will not open up is worth mentioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' strips the first letter, P, from PUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to voice or speak it aloud.

clue.text: Familiar figure in military HQ

explanation.surface: A well-known face is spotted at army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is a geometric shape, the familiar five-sided one, not a person; the building in Virginia housing the US defence department is named after its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided plane shape is a familiar geometric figure, and the US Department of Defense headquarters is a five-sided building of that name.

clue.text: Show places

parts.note: read as a noun phrase, places where shows are put on, rather than as a command to display locations

explanation.surface: A tour guide is told to point out the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb with 'places' as its object; read together they are buildings where shows are staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Playhouses are venues where plays and other shows are staged.

clue.text: Meal of chopped pears tin-opener needed

indicators.note: the pears are cut up, so their letters are broken and rearranged
the opener of the word tin is its first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for a dessert of cut-up tinned pears needs a can opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin-opener' looks like the kitchen gadget, but splits into 'tin' and 'opener': the first letter of tin, T, follows REPAS, the anagram of PEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Water-carrier met a prophet

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe that carries water

explanation.surface: Someone carrying water bumps into a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water-carrier' suggests a person with a bucket, or Aquarius; here it is a garden hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the Minor Prophets of the Hebrew Bible, with a book bearing his name.

clue.text: Executioner's sword ?

explanation.surface: The headsman's weapon is asked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': one who hangs people is a hanger, and a hanger is also a short sword once worn from the belt.
explanation.definitionFit: One who carries out death by the rope is literally a hanger, and the same word names a short curved sword hung at the belt.

clue.text: Knocks up rising Irish poet to find accommodation for guest

parts.note: to knock up in sport is to practise, and boxers spar when they practise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the poet's name is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Thomas Moore was the Irish poet of the Irish Melodies

explanation.surface: A man knocks on the door to wake an Irish poet so he can find a bed for a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MOORE into EROOM. 'Knocks up' is a practice session, as a knock-up in tennis is; a boxer's practice is sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom kept free in a house for visitors to sleep in.

clue.text: Tracts in the Far East

indicators.note: the letters needed are found inside the words Far East, running across them

explanation.surface: Regions of land in Asia are being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into the words 'Far East', which hold the run of letters across the space.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracts are expanses of land, regions or zones.

clue.text: Royal train, perhaps ?

parts.note: a train in the sense of a line of followers attending a monarch, rather than a railway train

explanation.surface: The monarch's private railway carriage is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests the railway; a train is also a body of attendants following a great person.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite of followers or attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Can return in long, boat

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the word for long

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: the word can comes back, read from end to start

explanation.surface: A tin can floats back in a long boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CAN into NAC, which 'in' places inside PINE. The comma after 'long' makes it look like an adjective for the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship, or a light sailing vessel.

clue.text: Girl gives song after Mr French

indicators.note: the song comes after the French title, so it follows it

parts.note: M is short for monsieur, the French for Mr
an aria is a song for a solo voice in an opera

explanation.surface: A girl sings for a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places ARIA after M, the abbreviation of monsieur.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: Insipid Hardy character without the least variety

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the heroine's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel

indicators.note: a variety of the word least is a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy heroine is dismissed as dull, lacking even the smallest variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: TESS wraps ASTEL, the anagram of LEAST made by 'variety'.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is insipid lacks flavour, having no savour at all.

clue.text: Measure of business done at the pastrycook's

explanation.surface: A shop's sales figures are being tallied at a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half points to a pastry: a folded pie of fruit-filled pastry sold at the baker's.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's total sales over a period are its takings, and a baker sells folded fruit pies of the same name.

clue.text: Artist uses odd term about trade-mark

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, round, the trade mark word
odd suggests the word term is in a strange order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a brand is a trade mark or brand name

explanation.surface: A painter signs his work with a strange logo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges TERM into REMT, and 'about' puts it round BRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was the great Dutch painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Sounds like a river horse

indicators.note: the answer is said the same way as the river's name when spoken

parts.note: the Rhone is a river flowing through Switzerland and France

explanation.surface: A hippopotamus, the river horse, makes a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river horse' is the hippo's name, but 'a river' and 'horse' are two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed through a darker colour.

clue.text: A leading light, naturally

parts.note: an eminent person is a leading light, but here it is a natural light in the sky that leads travellers

explanation.surface: Someone is praised as an obvious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading light' means a prominent figure; 'naturally' makes it a light in nature that guides navigators north.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, has long been the guide by which sailors steer.

clue.text: Herb found by simple' hill-dweller in interior

indicators.note: one word sits in the interior, the inside, of the other

parts.note: plain means simple, without decoration
an ant lives in an anthill

explanation.surface: A medicinal plant is discovered by a simple mountain dweller deep inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hill-dweller' suggests a hill farmer; it is an ant in its anthill, placed inside PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain is a common low-growing plant used in folk medicine.

clue.text: So two cats go wild 'with this playing style

indicators.note: the letters go wild, scattering into a fresh order

parts.note: two copies of the word cat

explanation.surface: A pair of cats run amok in a musician's practice room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wild' rearranges SO and CAT twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for detached, clipped notes, a manner of performing.

clue.text: Epstein work the Muhammadan ruler returned

indicators.note: the ruler's title is turned round and read from end to start

parts.note: an amir or emir is a ruler in the Muslim world

explanation.surface: A sculpture is given back by an Islamic prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Epstein's relief of Rima, heroine of W. H. Hudson's Green Mansions, stands in Hyde Park, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Epstein carved the figure of Rima, the bird-girl of Hudson's novel, as a memorial in Hyde Park.

clue.text: Perhaps the senior resident is Dr Mole-it could be

indicators.note: the letters of the doctor's name and it could be made into other words if rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the oldest inhabitant might be a doctor called Mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DRMOLE and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran who has lived somewhere a long time is the area's senior resident.

clue.text: Not a rule to upset this angler

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the run of letters reads backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Breaking the rules is not the fisherman's way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to upset' turns NOT and LAW together, giving WAL then TON. Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Izaak Walton, author of The Compleat Angler, is the most famous fisherman in English literature.

clue.text: Sort of grit one's found in a river.

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the word grit is sorted into another order

parts.note: one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A kind of grit turns up in a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges GRIT into TIGR. 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tigris flows through Turkey and Iraq, one of the two rivers of Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Transport people make a bloomer

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Commuters make a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; here it is a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnation is a garden flower, and a bloomer is something that blooms.

clue.text: Firm raised money by a masque

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A company raises funds through an entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SUM into MUS. Milton's Comus is the best-known English masque.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Comus is a masque, a courtly entertainment of verse, music and dance.

clue.text: Song must first be played ?

parts.note: a round for voices where each singer takes up the tune in turn, so the first part must be sung before the next voice can join in

explanation.surface: A musician insists a certain number opens the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: A round-song in which voices take up the tune one after another; the next singer must catch up the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A round for three or more voices, popular in the seventeenth century, often with comic words.

clue.text: Mark II

explanation.surface: A second version of something is labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is the first name of the American writer Mark Twain; 'twain' is also an old word for two, written II in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens wrote as Mark Twain, and twain is an archaic word for the number two.

clue.text: Senior schoolboy can enter room backwards

indicators.note: the whole result is then read backwards
the can enters, goes inside, the room

parts.note: taken as written
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A prefect can walk into a room in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' puts TIN inside ROOM, making ROTINOM, which 'backwards' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a monitor is a senior pupil given duties of supervision, like a prefect.

clue.text: Girl gets man, kind of square, hard type.

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler

explanation.surface: A girl lands a man who is a bit of a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' suggests a dull person; it is the T-square used in technical drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was once the name of a legendary stone of supreme hardness.

clue.text: Stuff mined in 'Cape Province, perhaps ?

parts.note: Cape Province is part of South Africa, abbreviated SA
tin is a metal that is mined

explanation.surface: A mineral is dug up in a part of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means cloth here, not material dug from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and satin is a glossy fabric.

clue.text: Drink now 'mixed in separate container

indicators.note: the mixed letters go in the word for separate, which acts as their container

parts.note: to sunder is to separate

indicators.note: the word now is mixed into another order

explanation.surface: A drink is now stirred into a separate glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges NOW into OWN, which 'in' places inside SUNDER, the 'container'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset.
